newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH SIDES OVERCOME SCOTS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH SIDES OVERCOME SCOTS.

text.p: French sides Dax and Brive overcame Scotland's Edinburgh and Caledonia respectively in contrasting styles on Sunday in their European Cup pool matches.
In Dax, international centre Richard Dourthe contributed 34 points as Dax crushed Edinburgh 69-12 while in Perth Brive struggled to defeat Caledonia 32-30.
Dourthe, suspended for two months last season for rough play and warned again in an international against Wales this month, scored three tries and kicked a further 19 points.
The victory allowed Dax, who scored 10 tries in all, to move to the top of Pool A alongside Welsh side Pontypridd. Dax travel to Bath next Saturday.

"I was under pressure to do well today after being criticised in the Wales match. We needed to score as many points as possible because I feel that Pontypridd, Bath and Dax will all end up with three wins," Dourthe said.
"Now we hope to win the match in Bath so as to play our quarter-final in Dax."
Caledonia, most impressive of the Scottish districts in the Cup, conceded converted tries to wingers Gareld Fabre and Sebastien Carrat in the opening 10 minutes.
"We were staring at a 50 points defeat after the opening few minutes," said Caledonia coach Ian Rankin.
Caledonia hauled themselves back into contention with two penalties from Scotland full-back Rowen Shepherd and a converted try by lock Stuart Grimes.
But after Shepherd left the field at halftime, Brive regained control through a penalty followed by a converted try from prop Didier Casedei and held on to win narrowly.
